title: two-phase-decode-tentative-routing-score-calibration-and-graceful-retreat-plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a two-phase speculative decode flow that starts decoding early using a lightweight tentative route and either commits emitted tokens from the tentative path or gracefully retreats to the canonical model when acceptance metrics fall below calibrated thresholds. This ticket covers design-to-implementation for routing heuristics, acceptance scoring, KV-cache reconciliation, rollback semantics for partially emitted tokens, and operator-facing controls for tuning cost/latency trade-offs.
background: We currently pay the latency cost of full prefill before decoding for many workloads. Prior experiments indicate a fast, quantized tentative model (Q8/float16 hybrid) can produce early tokens for a majority of short-turn requests with high agreement to the full model, reducing p50 latency and cost. However, past attempts lacked robust acceptance metrics to decide when to commit tentative outputs and to safe-fallback without user-visible inconsistencies. Kernel selection and attention variants (FlashAttention v2, sliding-window) interact with tentative prefill timing and KV cache layout; we must account for kernel-induced probability shifts and KV cache rewriting costs when switching mid-stream.
proposed_solution: Introduce a runtime component 'two-phase-conductor' with stages: 1) Tentative route selection: lightweight fingerprinting of the request (seq_len, model_family, prompt_category) selects a tentative model variant and a prefill probe budget. 2) Prefill probe: run a shallow prefill on tentative route to populate a provisional KV cache and produce an early hypothesis for the first N tokens. 3) Acceptance scoring: compute an acceptance score using a small set of metrics (per-token logit delta, mean per-token KL between tentative and a small verifier head, top-k overlap) plus operational signals (latency budget, cost_budget_remaining). 4) Decision: if score >= accept_threshold -> commit tentative outputs and continue on tentative execution path; else -> fallback to canonical model with KV cache reconciliation and possible rollback of emitted tokens. 5) Graceful retreat: when falling back mid-output, emit a replacement event stream with token replacement markers and optional application-level deduplication hints. The conductor exposes tunables: accept_threshold, probe_window_tokens, verifier_sample_rate, fallback_mode (hot-swap vs full-reprefill), and kernel_hint (prefer flash-attn/gemm for large context). Kernel selection logic will prefer faster kernels when tentative route is enabled but will bias toward numerically stable kernels for verifier runs.
runtime_config_changes: Add new config section 'speculative_decoding' to runtime config: enable: boolean; accept_threshold: float; probe_window: int; verifier_model: string; fallback_mode: string (options: 're-prefill', 'hot-swap'); kv_reconcile_policy: string (options: 'merge', 'discard'); kernel_hint_priority: list of kernels. Surface these in Dedicated/Private as toggles with safe defaults. Add telemetry flags to trace acceptance decisions per-request.
acceptance_criteria: Functional: Successful end-to-end path where tentative path is accepted and tokens emitted are identical to canonical model in >= 98% of accepted requests for a TINY prompt workload (<=64 tokens).
Latency: p50 generation latency reduced by >= 20% on the 'short-turn' benchmark suite when speculative_decoding.enable=true and default params used.
Cost: token compute-hours for short-turn workload reduced by >= 15% at 95% produced token quality parity.
Safety: No user-observable token corruption in fallback scenarios; unit tests covering rollback for sequences with partially emitted tokens pass.
Observability: Telemetry emits acceptance_score, tentative_model_id, verifier_sampled=true|false, fallback_reason and KV_reconcile_action for all speculative-enabled requests.
Config: Admin UI exposes accept_threshold and probe_window with recommended ranges and 'dry-run' mode where accept decisions are logged but not applied.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: feature flag behind org opt-in + dry-run that logs decisions but never commits tentative tokens (1 week). Stage 1: Canary on internal non-critical customers with accept_threshold conservative (0.99) and verifier_sample_rate=100% (2 weeks). Stage 2: Expand to broader canary with default thresholds, verifier_sample_rate=10% and monitor metrics for regressions (3 weeks). Stage 3: Gradual ramp by traffic percent with A/B comparing production baseline; enable kernel_hint optimizations only after numeric stability verified. Stage 4: GA and enable for self-serve by default with editable controls in Console. Abort criteria: sustained p95 latency regression >5% or unexplained drop in token-quality metrics.
testing_plan: Unit tests: acceptance scorer edge-cases (empty logits, truncated cache), KV reconcile policies.
Integration tests: simulated early-accept and mid-output-fallback flows with deterministic RNG to validate token-stream consistency and rollback markers.
Load tests: run short-turn and long-context mixes through canary infra to measure kernel interplay and tail latency.
A/B experiments: measure user-visible text-quality metrics (n-gram overlap, KL proxies) on logged prompts between speculative-on and control groups.
Chaos test: force verifier_model mismatch and kernel fallback scenarios to ensure graceful retreat and clean metric signals.
risks: Numeric drift between tentative and canonical model variants due to quantization and kernel differences causing false accepts.
KV cache reconciliation complexity leading to increased tail latency on fallback paths.
Application-visible duplication or missing tokens if rollback protocol not correctly applied in streaming clients.
Operator confusion from too many tunables; potential misconfiguration causing increased cost.
Edge-case prompts where tentative model hallucinates rare tokens leading to user-facing regressions.
mitigations: Conservative default thresholds and 100% verifier sampling during early canaries.
Implement a fast-path 'atomic-replace' for small KV merges to reduce tail latency during fallback.
Define clear streaming contract: runtime emits a 'retcon' marker when tokens are replaced; SDKs updated to handle retcon deterministically.
Provide pre-made configuration profiles in Console (balanced, aggressive, safe) to reduce operator error.
Run retrospective evals on top-k overlap slices to find prompt categories prone to mismatch and add explicit routing exceptions.

console/team -- UI controls for speculative_decoding config
